definition_zh: 使困惑；难住；阻碍（声、光等）
definition_en: to confuse completely; also, to impede or deflect something such as sound or light
core_image: 一道考题让全班集体停笔，面面相觑
scene: 钟声敲了三下，草稿纸写满三页，答案还是没影。The trick question baffled even the top students.
sceneCN: 这里 baffle 指「难住、使困惑」（第 1 个义项：令人完全不解）；句意：这道怪题把尖子生也难住了。

senses.title: To confuse completely
senses.definition: to leave someone unable to understand or explain
senses.definitionCN: 使人无法理解或解释
senses.example: The motive baffled the detectives.
senses.exampleCN: 作案动机让侦探们一头雾水。
senses.why: The older sense was public disgrace; confusion inherited the helplessness.
senses.whyCN: 旧义是当众受挫；「困惑」继承了那份无力感。

senses.title: To defeat or frustrate efforts
senses.definition: to prevent someone from achieving an aim
senses.definitionCN: 使人达不到目的
senses.example: Mountain weather baffled every rescue attempt.
senses.exampleCN: 山区天气让每次营救都归于失败。
senses.why: The earliest English meaning was to defeat openly, as in battle.
senses.whyCN: 最早的英语义是公开挫败，尤指在战场上。

senses.title: To impede sound or light
senses.definition: to check or deflect waves, as a baffle plate in an engine or studio
senses.definitionCN: 阻遏或导偏波动，如发动机或录音棚里的挡板
senses.example: Foam baffles the echo in the recording booth.
senses.exampleCN: 吸音棉消除了录音间里的回声。
senses.why: Technical English reused the defeating sense for waves.
senses.whyCN: 技术英语把「挫败」义转用于波动。

senses.title: To hinder movement, as terrain
senses.definition: of ground, weather, or obstacles, to slow and disorder movement
senses.definitionCN: 指地形、天气或障碍使行进迟滞混乱
senses.example: Drifts baffled the sledges for two days.
senses.exampleCN: 积雪阻滞雪橇达两天之久。
senses.why: Explorers' prose kept the old military sense alive.
senses.whyCN: 探险文学让古老的军事义得以存活。

senses.title: Baffling, as a mystery
senses.definition: in participial adjective use, hard or impossible to fathom
senses.definitionCN: 分词形容词用法，指难以捉摸
senses.example: The baffle disappearance filled the newspapers.
senses.exampleCN: 这桩离奇失踪案占据了各大报纸。
senses.why: The participle packages the confusion as a quality.
senses.whyCN: 分词把「困惑」打包成一种性质。

senses.title: To hoodwink in older use
senses.definition: in older English, to cheat or trick someone
senses.definitionCN: 旧式英语中指欺骗、耍弄
senses.example: Sharpers baffled green recruits out of their pay.
senses.exampleCN: 老骗子骗光了新兵的饷银。
senses.why: An obsolete sense that shows the word's rough origins.
senses.whyCN: 这个废义显露了该词粗粝的出身。

senses.title: Baffles, as equipment
senses.definition: plates or screens that check flow, in machines, tanks, or chimneys
senses.definitionCN: 机器、水箱、烟道中阻流导偏的板片
senses.example: Clean the baffles before the annual inspection.
senses.exampleCN: 年检前先把挡板清理干净。
senses.why: The verb became the name of the thing that does it.
senses.whyCN: 动词转而命名行使该功能之物。

senses.title: In astronomy, stray-light control
senses.definition: structures that block stray light inside telescopes
senses.definitionCN: 望远镜内阻挡杂散光的结构
senses.example: The baffle keeps starlight from fogging the sensor.
senses.exampleCN: 遮光罩防止星光照糊传感器。
senses.why: Optics borrowed the engineering word for light-control.
senses.whyCN: 光学借工程术语命名控光结构。

intro.en: Baffle is of uncertain origin; it appears in the sixteenth century meaning to disgrace publicly, possibly from a lost Scottish or French source, and perhaps related to bawdle or a French term for mockery; the modern senses of defeat and confusion grew from that public shaming.
intro.cn: baffle 词源不确定；16 世纪已见，义为「当众使其蒙羞」，或出自已失传的苏格兰语或法语词，一说与表示嘲弄的词相关；「挫败」「困惑」诸义均由「公开羞辱」发展而来。

items.en: Baffle is first recorded meaning to disgrace by sham treatment, as hanging a traitor in effigy.
items.cn: baffle 最早见于记载，指以羞辱性方式使其蒙羞，如对叛国者行绞刑草人。

items.en: Early evidence comes from Scottish records describing punishment of nobles.
items.cn: 早期例证出自苏格兰文献，述及对贵族的羞辱性惩处。

items.en: One theory links it to French beffler, to mock or deceive; another to bafouer.
items.cn: 一说联系法语 beffler「嘲弄、欺骗」，另一说联系 bafouer「嘲弄」。

items.en: The military sense, to defeat and frustrate, hardened in Civil War prose.
items.cn: 17 世纪英国内战文献中「挫败」义定型。

items.en: The mental sense, to confuse, became dominant as prose polished it.
items.cn: 18、19 世纪「使困惑」义渐成主导。

items.en: Engineering coined the baffle plate, and the noun spread through technology.
items.cn: 工程学造出 baffle plate（挡板），名词随技术扩散。

note.en: Group one gathers mock-theory cousins and sound-alikes; group two gathers confusion and hindrance words.
note.cn: 第一组收「嘲弄说」近亲与音近词；第二组收困惑与阻碍义场的词。

root: 词源不确定。16 世纪（约 1560 年代）已见，本义「以羞辱方式使其蒙耻」，早期例证多出自苏格兰文献（如对贵族行草人刑）；或与法语 beffler「嘲弄、欺骗」、bafouer「讥讽」相关。17 世纪发展出「挫败」义，18、19 世纪「使困惑」义成为主流，近代工程学又造出挡板（baffle）一义。

abstract.cn: 想象一捆用绳扎起的包裹。

abstract.en: See a traveller dragging a heavy load.
abstract.cn: 想象一名旅客拖着沉重的行装。

examples.en: We waited by the belt for our baggage.
examples.cn: 我们在传送带旁等自己的行李。

examples.en: She carried a lot of emotional baggage from her childhood.
examples.cn: 她背负着许多来自童年的情感包袱。

examples.en: The airline lost his baggage on the way home.
examples.cn: 航空公司在他回家的路上弄丢了他的行李。

dict_mnemonic.text: bag 是包，加 -age 表示集合：许多包捆在一起，就是 baggage 行李。

root: 来自古法语 bagage「一捆货物」，与 bag 同源；进入英语后指旅人的全部行装，因不可数而常说 a piece of baggage，近代又引申为「精神包袱」。

sensesIntro.en: The whole load a traveller carries and the weight a person carries inside share one word.
sensesIntro.cn: 旅人随身带的整批行装，与人心里背负的重量，共用一个词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a worn case circling on a belt.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只旧箱子在传送带上转圈。

branches.en: checked baggage
baggage claim
excess baggage
emotional baggage
carry old baggage

intro.en: The -age suffix turns bag into a collective noun for all the bags.
intro.cn: 后缀 -age 把 bag 变成表示全部行李的集合名词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; the word came from Old French bagage.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，这个词来自古法语 bagage。

items.meaning: all the bags of a traveller
as much as a bag holds

definition_zh: n. 风笛（用臂下气囊供气、带低音管的簧管乐器，常用复数）；风笛声；风笛乐曲
definition_en: a wind instrument in which air pressed from a bag under the arm sounds reed pipes, usually used in the plural; the sound or music of this instrument
core_image: 臂下夹着鼓鼓的气囊、肩上斜插三根低音管的那副乐器
scene: 婚礼上新娘进场时，山坡上响起了风笛。On the hillside the bagpipes sounded as the bride walked in.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：这里 bagpipes 指风笛发出的声音，而不是乐器本身；句意是新娘进场时山坡上传来笛声。

forms.label: 复数（英语中通常以复数出现）

derivatives.zh: （风笛的）低音持续管；持续低音

senses.title: The instrument itself
senses.definition: a musical instrument whose reed pipes are sounded by air squeezed from a bag held under the arm
senses.definitionCN: 一种簧管乐器，靠挤压夹在臂下的气囊供气发声
senses.example: He carried a set of bagpipes wrapped in green cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 他抱着一副用绿布包好的风笛。
senses.why: The name is literally bag plus pipe, so it describes how the instrument is fed with air rather than how it looks.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面就是「袋」加「管」，因此描述的是供气方式，而不是外形。

senses.title: The sound it makes
senses.definition: the loud reedy sound of the instrument, or a tune played on it
senses.definitionCN: 这件乐器响亮带簧质的声音，或用它吹出的曲子
senses.example: The bagpipes drifted across the water before the boats came in.
senses.exampleCN: 船还没进港，风笛声先掠过水面传了过来。
senses.why: English lets an instrument name stand for its sound, so the plural can mean the music rather than the object.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许乐器名代指其声音，所以复数形式可以指乐声而非实物。

intro.en: Bagpipe is a plain English compound: bag plus pipe. The instrument is ancient, but the English name is a medieval description of how it is blown.
intro.cn: bagpipe 是一个朴素的英语复合词：bag「袋」加 pipe「管」。乐器本身很古老，但这个英语名字是中世纪对吹奏方式的直白描述。

items.en: Herders in the Near East already blew reed pipes fed by an animal-skin air bag.
items.cn: 近东的牧人早已用兽皮气囊供气吹响簧管。

items.en: Roman writers describe a pipe played with a bag, the tibia utricularis.
items.cn: 罗马作家记载过一种用气囊吹奏的管乐器 tibia utricularis。

items.en: Old English pipe meant a tube or a musical pipe, from Latin pipare, to chirp.
items.cn: 古英语 pipe 指管子或管乐器，源自拉丁语 pipare「啾鸣」。

items.en: Middle English joins bagge and pipe into baggepipe, the bag-blown pipe.
items.cn: 中古英语把 bagge「袋」与 pipe「管」合成 baggepipe，即用袋吹的管。

items.en: Scottish players fix the form with a chanter and drones, and the Highland pipe becomes a national emblem.
items.cn: 苏格兰乐手确立了指孔管加低音管的形制，高地风笛成为民族象征。

items.en: Army pipe bands carry the word worldwide, and the plural bagpipes becomes the usual form.
items.cn: 军中风笛队把这个词带到世界各地，复数 bagpipes 成为常用形式。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps other bag- and pipe- words so the compound stays visible; the near-meaning group names the parts of the instrument and its reed relatives.
note.cn: 形近组保留其他带 bag- 与 pipe- 的词，让这个复合结构一直看得见；近义组列出这件乐器的构件及其簧管亲属。

entries.definition: A row of tubes of different lengths.
entries.definitionCN: 一排长短不同的管子组成的乐器。

entries.definition: A long line carrying oil or gas.
entries.definitionCN: 输送石油或天然气的长管道。

entries.definition: Cases and bags taken on a journey.
A long thin loaf of French bread.
The pipe on which the tune is fingered.
entries.definitionCN: 用来按出旋律的那根管。

entries.definition: A pipe giving one unchanging low note.
An old wind instrument and the dance for it.
entries.definitionCN: 一种古老管乐器，也指配它的舞蹈。

entries.definition: An orchestral double-reed woodwind.
entries.definitionCN: 管弦乐队中的双簧木管乐器。

normalIntro.en: Bagpipe is bag plus pipe: a bag of air feeding a set of pipes. Hold that picture and the word never needs memorising.
normalIntro.cn: bagpipe 就是 bag「袋」加 pipe「管」：一袋空气喂养一组管子。记住这幅画面，这个词就不必硬背。

normal.en: Picture a leather bag squeezed under one arm.
normal.cn: 想象一只皮囊夹在一条臂下被挤压。

normal.en: Three long pipes stick up over the shoulder.
normal.cn: 三根长管斜插在肩头上方。

normal.en: One short pipe takes the melody under the fingers.
normal.cn: 一根短管在指下奏出旋律。

normal.en: The bag keeps the sound going while the player breathes.
normal.cn: 吹奏者换气时，气囊让声音不断。

normal.en: Bag plus pipe equals bagpipe, and the plural is bagpipes.
normal.cn: bag 加 pipe 就是 bagpipe，复数是 bagpipes。

abstract.en: A stored breath that outlasts a single lungful.
abstract.cn: 一份存起来的气息，比一口气更长久。

abstract.en: One steady note under a moving tune.
abstract.cn: 流动的曲调之下垫着一个不动的音。

abstract.en: A whole country carried in a cloth bag.
abstract.cn: 一个民族被装进一只布袋里带走。

examples.en: The bagpipes struck up as the coffin left the church.
examples.cn: 棺木离开教堂时，风笛奏了起来。

examples.en: She learned the bagpipes at twelve and never put them down.
examples.cn: 她十二岁学风笛，此后一直没放下。

examples.en: A lone piper stood on the rock above the bay.
examples.cn: 一名风笛手独自站在海湾上方的岩石上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：bag「袋子」+ pipe「管子」——臂下夹着一袋气去吹一组管子，就是 bagpipe 风笛；因为管子不止一根，英语里常说 bagpipes。

root: 英语 bag「袋」与 pipe「管」直接复合；pipe 上溯拉丁语 pipare「啾鸣」。乐器本身源自古代近东的兽皮气囊簧管，中古英语约 1400 年造出 baggepipe 这个名字，苏格兰高地确立形制后随军乐队传遍世界。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses, one object: the instrument you carry, and the sound that carries across a valley.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项，同一件东西：你抱着走的乐器，以及能越过整条山谷的声音。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a full air bag under one arm with long pipes over the shoulder
core.cn: 核心意象：一臂之下夹着饱满气囊，长管斜插肩头

branches.en: A cloth-wrapped set on the knee.
branches.cn: 膝上放着一副布包的乐器。

branches.en: Fingers working the short melody pipe.
branches.cn: 手指在短旋律管上按动。

branches.en: A thin cry across the water.
branches.cn: 掠过水面的一声细长鸣响。

branches.en: A slow lament at a graveside.
The bag that keeps both going.
branches.cn: 让实物与声音都不断的那只气囊。

intro.en: Bagpipe is built from two whole English words, so its parts are roots rather than prefixes; the endings below show how the family grows around it.
intro.cn: bagpipe 由两个完整的英语词构成，因此其构件是词根而非前缀；下面这些词尾展示这个词族如何扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer sits behind pipe: pipare, to chirp, and the Roman bag-fed pipe called tibia utricularis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次藏在 pipe 之后：pipare「啾鸣」，以及罗马那种以囊供气的管乐器 tibia utricularis。

latinEntries.exampleCN: tibia 指罗马的一种管乐器。

definition_zh: n. 饵；诱饵；诱人上钩之物　v. 装饵于；下饵诱捕；故意激怒、逗弄
definition_en: food or a lure used to attract fish or animals; something that tempts a person into a trap; to put bait on or in; to deliberately annoy or provoke
core_image: 钩尖上那一小块颤动的鱼肉，水下有东西正盯着它
scene: 老渔夫往钩上挂了一小块鱼肉。The old fisherman put a strip of fish on the hook as bait.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bait 指引鱼上钩的食物；句意是老渔夫把一小条鱼肉挂在钩上当饵。

collocations.zh: 诱饵调包（先用低价引人再换货的销售手法）

forms.label: 第三人称单数／名词复数

senses.title: Food that lures
senses.definition: food placed on a hook or in a trap to attract fish or animals
senses.definitionCN: 放在钩上或陷阱里用来引鱼、引兽的食物
senses.example: He dug worms for bait before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天亮前他挖了些蚯蚓当饵。
senses.why: The Old Norse source meant to make an animal bite, so the noun names whatever produces that bite.
senses.whyCN: 古诺斯语词源意为「使动物咬」，因此这个名词指能引出那一咬的东西。

senses.title: A tempting offer
senses.definition: something attractive offered so that a person will do what someone else wants
senses.definitionCN: 为让人按他人意愿行事而抛出的诱人条件
senses.example: The free trial was bait for a yearly contract.
senses.exampleCN: 免费试用只是引人签年度合同的诱饵。
senses.why: The fishing picture transfers to people: the offer is the worm, and the contract is the hook.
senses.whyCN: 钓鱼的画面被移用到人身上：优惠是那条虫，合同才是钩。

senses.title: To put bait on
senses.definition: to place food on a hook or in a trap, or to set a trap with food
senses.definitionCN: 把食物挂在钩上或放进陷阱，或用食物布置陷阱
senses.example: She baited the line and cast it past the reeds.
senses.exampleCN: 她给钓线装好饵，把钩甩过芦苇丛。
senses.why: English turns the noun into a verb with no change of form, a very common shift in the language.
senses.whyCN: 英语不改词形就把名词转为动词，这在该语言中极为常见。

senses.title: To provoke on purpose
senses.definition: to deliberately annoy or attack someone, especially to make them lose control
senses.definitionCN: 故意招惹或攻击某人，尤指使其失去自控
senses.example: The lawyer tried to bait the witness into shouting.
senses.exampleCN: 律师试图激怒证人，让他喊起来。
senses.why: An older sport set dogs on a chained animal; the same verb now describes needling a person until they snap.
senses.whyCN: 旧时有一种放犬撕咬拴住动物的把戏；同一个动词如今指把人撩到失控。

intro.en: Bait is a causative of bite: the Old Norse source meant to make something bite. From that single idea come the worm, the tempting offer, and the deliberate provocation.
intro.cn: bait 是 bite「咬」的使役形式：古诺斯语词源意为「使某物咬」。由这一个念头，生出鱼虫、诱饵与故意挑怒三层意思。

items.en: The deep root bheid meant to split or bite into, the same source as bite.
items.cn: 深层词根 bheid 意为劈开或咬入，与 bite 同源。

items.en: Germanic baitjan was a causative of bitan, so it meant to make something bite.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 baitjan 是 bitan 的使役形式，意为「使……咬」。

items.en: Old Norse beita meant to hunt with dogs, to pasture, and to feed a hook.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 beita 指用犬追猎、放牧，也指给钩上食。

items.en: Middle English beyt names food set out to make a fish or animal bite.
items.cn: 中古英语 beyt 指为使鱼或兽咬钩而摆出的食物。

items.en: Writers extend the word to any lure that tempts a person into a trap.
items.cn: 文人把该词扩展为任何诱人入局的诱惑物。

items.en: A second verb sense appears, to torment a chained animal, and later to needle a person.
items.cn: 又生出第二个动词义：折磨被拴住的动物，后来指故意激怒他人。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the same-sound bate and three rhymes; the near-meaning group covers the wider vocabulary of luring, from a false bird to thrown fish scraps.
note.cn: 形近组放同音的 bate 与三个押韵词；近义组覆盖「引诱」这一更大的词汇场，从假鸟到撒入水中的碎鱼。

entries.definition: To hold back or reduce, as in bated breath.
entries.definitionCN: 抑制或减弱，如 bated breath「屏息」。

entries.definition: Money paid to free an accused person before trial.
To stay until something happens.
The way a person or animal walks.
Anything that attracts and draws someone in.
entries.definitionCN: 任何吸引并引人入内之物。

entries.definition: A false figure used to draw birds or attention.
entries.definitionCN: 用来引鸟或转移注意的假物。

entries.definition: Something offered to persuade.
Chopped fish thrown in the water to attract fish.
entries.definitionCN: 撒入水中引鱼的碎鱼饵。

normalIntro.en: Bait hides inside bite: change one vowel and you get the thing that makes a fish bite.
normalIntro.cn: bait 就藏在 bite 里：换一个元音，就得到那个「让鱼咬」的东西。

normal.en: Bite is what the fish does; bait is what you offer.
normal.cn: bite 是鱼做的动作，bait 是你递出的东西。

normal.en: A worm on a hook is bait in its first sense.
normal.cn: 钩上的蚯蚓是第一义的 bait。

normal.en: A free gift with a hidden contract is bait in its second sense.
normal.cn: 附赠礼品背后藏着合同，那是第二义的 bait。

normal.en: To bait a hook is to load it; to bait a person is to load them too.
normal.cn: bait a hook 是给钩装料，bait a person 是给人「装料」点火。

normal.en: Take the bait means swallow the hook along with the worm.
normal.cn: take the bait 就是连钩带虫一起吞下。

abstract.en: A small kindness with a sharp curve inside.
abstract.cn: 一点小小的善意，里面藏着一道尖锐的弯。

abstract.en: The visible part of an invisible arrangement.
abstract.cn: 一桩看不见的安排里，唯一看得见的那部分。

abstract.en: Anger offered as food until someone bites.
abstract.cn: 把怒气当食物递出去，直到有人咬下。

examples.en: The trout ignored the bait and drifted away.
examples.cn: 那条鳟鱼没理鱼饵，慢慢游开了。

examples.en: He baited the trap with a piece of cheese.
examples.cn: 他用一块奶酪给陷阱下了饵。

examples.en: Reporters baited her for hours, but she stayed calm.
examples.cn: 记者们撩了她几个小时，她始终平静。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「贝特」——把宝贝特意摆出来给你看，其实是 bait 诱饵。再记字形：bait 与 bite 只差一个元音，「让它咬」的东西就是饵。

root: 出自原始日耳曼语使役形式 baitjan「使咬」，与 bite 同源；古诺斯语 beita 兼有追猎、放牧、给钩上食三义，约 1300 年进入中古英语作 beyt。1590 年代生出「诱人入局」的比喻义，17 世纪又生出「故意激怒」的动词义。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses share one move: put something tempting in front of a creature and wait for it to bite.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项共用同一个动作：把一个诱人的东西摆到某个生物面前，然后等它咬下来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a strip of fish trembling on a hook while something watches from below
core.cn: 核心意象：钩尖上一小条颤动的鱼肉，水下有东西正盯着

branches.en: A tin of worms in the mud.
A free month with a year attached.
branches.cn: 免费一个月，后面拴着一整年。

branches.en: A thumb pressing food onto the barb.
A question aimed at a sore spot.
branches.cn: 专往痛处戳的一句提问。

branches.en: The hook nobody is meant to see.
branches.cn: 那根谁都不该看见的钩。

intro.en: Bait has no prefix of its own; it is a bare Germanic root. The endings below build its verb forms and the wider vocabulary of tempting.
intro.cn: bait 本身没有前缀，是一个赤裸的日耳曼语词根。下面这些词缀构成它的动词形式，以及「引诱」这一语义场的更大词汇。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer arrives through the near-synonyms: entice and entrap carry en-, and enticement carries -ment.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是通过近义词进来的：entice 与 entrap 带 en-，enticement 带 -ment。

latinEntries.exampleCN: captare 是 capture 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Illicere gives illicit charm in old texts.
latinEntries.exampleCN: illicere 在旧文献中表引诱之意。
esca 在拉丁语中意为饵。

definition_zh: 平衡；余额；使平衡；权衡
definition_en: a steady state, the money left in an account, or to keep something steady
core_image: 天平两端各放一只砝码，指针缓缓停住
scene: 收银台前，店员抬头看了看屏幕。Please check the balance on your card.
sceneCN: 这里 balance 是「余额」（第 2 个义项：账户里剩下的钱）；句意是请查看你卡里的余额。

derivatives.zh: 由 balance 加 -ed 构成，义为「均衡的；平稳的」
由 im- 加 balance 构成，义为「失衡」
由 balance 加 -ing 构成，义为「平衡；权衡」

senses.title: Steady position
senses.definition: a state in which weight is evenly spread and nothing falls
senses.definitionCN: 重量均匀分布、不会倒下的状态
senses.example: She kept her balance on the icy path.
senses.exampleCN: 她在结冰的小路上保持着平衡。
senses.why: Balance came from Latin bilanx, 'two scales', so its first sense is the equal weighing of two sides.
senses.whyCN: balance 来自拉丁语 bilanx「两架天平」，所以最初的义项是两边等重。

senses.title: Money left
senses.definition: the amount of money remaining in an account
senses.definitionCN: 账户中剩余的钱数
senses.example: Please check the balance on your card.
senses.exampleCN: 请查看你卡里的余额。
senses.why: A scale shows what is left after amounts are set against each other, so the word came to mean the money remaining.
senses.whyCN: 天平会显示两边相抵后剩下的量，于是这个词就用来指账户中剩余的钱。

senses.title: To weigh or steady
senses.definition: to keep something steady or to compare two needs
senses.definitionCN: 使某物保持稳定，或比较两方面的需求
senses.example: You must balance study and rest.
senses.exampleCN: 你必须平衡学习与休息。
senses.why: Holding scales level became a verb, and from weighing objects it extended to weighing competing demands.
senses.whyCN: 把天平端平变成了动词，并从称量物件扩展到权衡相互竞争的需求。

intro.en: Balance goes back to a Latin word for a pair of scales.
intro.cn: balance 可追溯到拉丁语中表示「一副天平」的词。

items.en: bilanx meant 'having two scales'.
items.cn: bilanx 意为「有两架天平」。

items.en: balance named a weighing device.
items.cn: balance 指称重器具。

items.en: the word entered English as a pair of scales.
items.cn: 这个词以「天平」之义进入英语。

items.en: balance gained the sense of money left over.
items.cn: balance 获得「结余」的义项。

items.en: balance covers steady states and fair choices.
items.cn: 如今 balance 涵盖稳定状态与公平取舍。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the opening bal-; the near-meaning group gives steadiness and what is left.
note.cn: 形近组都以 bal- 开头；近义组是稳定与剩余的说法。

entries.definition: a vote or a paper used to vote
heavy material that steadies a ship
a platform outside a window
a state of balance

definition_zh: adj. 秃头的；无发的；光秃的、磨平的；（陈述）直白的、不加掩饰的
definition_en: having little or no hair on the scalp; lacking natural covering or detail; plain and blunt, without softening
core_image: 帽子摘下后那片反着光的头顶
scene: 他摘下帽子，露出光亮的前额。He took off his cap and showed a bald crown that caught the light.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bald 指头上无发；句意是他摘帽后露出反光的秃顶。

senses.title: Without hair
senses.definition: having little or no hair on the head
senses.definitionCN: 头上很少或没有头发
senses.example: He went bald in his early thirties.
senses.exampleCN: 他三十出头就秃了。
senses.why: The Middle English form described a shining white patch on the head, and the sense narrowed to the bareness itself.
senses.whyCN: 中古英语形式描写头上一块发亮的白斑，词义后来收窄为「光秃」本身。

senses.title: Stripped of covering
senses.definition: lacking the natural or usual covering, such as hair, tread, or vegetation
senses.definitionCN: 缺少天然或惯常的覆盖物，如毛发、胎面花纹或植被
senses.example: The tyres were bald and the hillside was bare.
senses.exampleCN: 轮胎花纹磨平了，山坡也光秃秃的。
senses.why: Once bald means bare skin, any surface that has lost its layer can borrow the word.
senses.whyCN: 既然 bald 指裸露的皮肤，任何失去表层的表面都能借用这个词。

senses.title: Plain and blunt
senses.definition: stated without any attempt to soften or disguise it
senses.definitionCN: 陈述时不作任何缓和或掩饰
senses.example: It was a bald lie and everyone knew it.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个赤裸裸的谎言，人人都看得出来。
senses.why: Speech with nothing laid over it is bare in the same way as a head with no hair.
senses.whyCN: 不加覆盖的言语，与不长头发的头一样「赤裸」。

intro.en: Bald probably began as a word about colour, not hair: a shining white patch. From there it moved to bareness, and then to blunt speech.
intro.cn: bald 起初大概是讲颜色而非头发：一块发亮的白斑。由此转为「光秃」，再转为「言语直白」。

items.en: The root bhel meant to shine or gleam white, and it also gives blaze and bleach.
items.cn: 词根 bhel 意为发亮或呈白色，也衍生出 blaze 与 bleach。

items.en: Middle English balled describes a head marked by a shining white patch.
items.cn: 中古英语 balled 形容头上有一块发亮的白斑。

items.en: Welsh bal names a white streak on the forehead of a horse, a close match in sense.
items.cn: 威尔士语 bal 指马额上的白色条纹，词义十分接近。

items.en: The spelling settles as bald, and the meaning shifts from white patch to hairless.
items.cn: 拼写定为 bald，词义由「白斑」转为「无发」。

items.en: Writers use the word for any surface stripped of its natural cover, such as a bald hill.
items.cn: 文人用该词指任何失去天然覆盖的表面，如光秃的山丘。

items.en: A figurative sense grows: the word now marks a statement left blunt and unsoftened.
items.cn: 又生出比喻义：该词指陈述直白、不加缓和修饰。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on one-letter and one-vowel neighbours, bold above all; the near-meaning group splits into bare surfaces and blunt speech, matching the two extended senses.
note.cn: 形近组由只差一个字母或一个元音的邻居组成，尤其是 bold；近义组分为「裸露表面」与「言语直白」两支，正对应两个引申义。

senses.title: Voting in secret
senses.titleCN: 不记名投票：不让别人看见你选谁
senses.definition: a system in which people vote secretly, so that no one knows how each person voted
senses.definitionCN: 一种不公开各人选择的投票方式
senses.example: The union decided to use a ballot rather than a show of hands.
senses.exampleCN: 工会决定采用不记名投票，而不是举手表决。
senses.why: The word began as the name of the little ball dropped into a box; the secrecy of that drop became the name of the whole method.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指投进箱子的小球；这种不让人看见的投法，后来成了整套制度的名字。

senses.title: The paper slip
senses.titleCN: 选票纸：承载一个人选择的那张纸
senses.definition: the printed paper on which a voter marks a choice
senses.definitionCN: 投票人在上面标记选择的印刷纸片
senses.example: She folded the ballot and pushed it through the slot.
senses.exampleCN: 她把选票折好，塞进投票口的缝里。
senses.why: From the ball to the paper: the object that carries one person's choice keeps the name.
senses.whyCN: 从小球到纸片：承载一个人选择的那件东西沿用同一个名字。

senses.title: The counted total
senses.titleCN: 投票总数：所有票加起来的数目或结果
senses.definition: the total number of votes recorded in an election, or the result they produce
senses.definitionCN: 一次选举中记录下来的全部票数，或这些票造成的结果
senses.example: He won the ballot by a narrow margin.
senses.exampleCN: 他以微弱优势赢得了这次投票。
senses.why: A ballot is also the count: once the slips are in the box, the word shifts from the container to the sum inside it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也可以指计票：纸片进了箱子之后，词义就从容器转指箱内的总数。

senses.title: The right to vote
senses.titleCN: 投票权：投出那一票的资格
senses.definition: the right to vote, or the act of exercising that right
senses.definitionCN: 投票的权利，或行使这项权利的行为
senses.example: Women fought for the ballot for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 女性为争取投票权奋斗了几十年。
senses.why: Possession of a ballot slip implies permission to cast it, so the object came to stand for the right itself.
senses.whyCN: 手里有选票就意味着有权投出它，于是这件实物也代表了权利本身。

senses.title: The list of candidates
senses.titleCN: 候选人名单：供人挑选的那份名单
senses.definition: the list of candidates or measures that voters may choose among
senses.definitionCN: 供选民从中选择的候选人名单或议题清单
senses.example: Two new parties will be on the ballot in November.
senses.exampleCN: 两个新政党将出现在十一月的选票名单上。
senses.why: A ballot lists the choices before it records them; the sheet is both a menu and a tally.
senses.whyCN: 选票先列出可选项，再记录选择；一张纸既是菜单，也是计数表。

senses.title: Drawing lots
senses.titleCN: 抽签：从容器里摸出小球来决定
senses.definition: the old practice of deciding by drawing small balls or tokens from a container
senses.definitionCN: 旧时从容器中摸出小球或筹码来决定结果的作法
senses.example: In the old guild, officers were chosen by ballot from a bowl.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧时的行会里，执事是从碗中抽签选出的。
senses.why: Before paper, a ballot was a ball; drawing balls from a bowl was the original random method.
senses.whyCN: 在纸张之前，这个词指的就是一颗球；从碗里摸球，正是最早的随机决定法。

senses.title: To hold a ballot
senses.titleCN: 动词：组织一次投票表决
senses.definition: to ask a group of people to vote on an issue
senses.definitionCN: 让一群人就某个问题投票
senses.example: The committee balloted its members on the new rules.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会就新规则让成员投票表决。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb of arranging: to ballot is to put the question to a ballot.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为表示安排动作的动词：举行投票，就是把问题交给一次表决。

senses.title: To cast a vote by ballot
senses.titleCN: 动词：以不记名方式投票
senses.definition: to vote by marking a ballot paper and placing it in the ballot box
senses.definitionCN: 在选票上作记号并投入票箱来投票
senses.example: Every delegate balloted before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 每位代表都在中午前投了票。
senses.why: The verb names the act of using the paper, not the counting that follows.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词指使用那张纸的动作，而不是随后的计票。

intro.en: Ballot reached English through French from Italian ballotta 'little ball'. That Italian word is generally traced to a reconstructed Germanic word for a ball; what is clear is the box full of little balls.
intro.cn: 这个词经法语进入英语，法语又借自意大利语中表示「小球」的词。那个意大利词一般追溯到原始日耳曼语中表示「球」的重构形式；可以确定的是那只装满小球的投票箱。

items.en: Italian ballotta meant 'little ball', a diminutive of balla 'ball'. Words for a ball of similar shape exist across the Romance languages.
items.cn: 意大利语中表示「小球」的那个词，是「球」的指小形式。罗曼语各族中都有形状相近的「球」的说法。

items.en: In Venice and other Italian city-states, voters dropped small balls or tokens into a container to record a choice without showing it.
items.cn: 在威尼斯等意大利城邦，投票人把小圆球或筹码投进容器，以记录不公开的选择。

items.en: French borrowed the Italian word as ballotte, and English took the same word from French in the same period.
items.cn: 法语借入这个意大利词，英语又在同一时期从法语借入同一个词。

items.en: The earliest English records show the word as the little ball used in voting; the paper-slip meaning appears considerably later.
items.cn: 英语最早记录中，这个词指投票用的小球；纸片选票的意思出现得晚得多。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the word meant the paper slip and the whole secret method, and the verb followed. The first recorded dates are approximate.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，这个词已指选票纸与整套无记名投票方式，动词用法也随之出现。首见年代为大致估计。

note.en: The first group looks similar in spelling or sound; the second group is close in meaning. None of the look-alikes shares the Italian origin.
note.cn: 第一组在拼写或读音上相近；第二组意思接近。第一组里的词没有一个是同一个意大利来源。

entries.definitionCN: 压舱物；词尾不同，来源是日耳曼语，不是意大利语。

entries.definition: a narrative song or poem; it ends differently and comes from Old French, not Italian
entries.definitionCN: 叙事歌谣；词尾不同，来自古法语，不是意大利语。

entries.definition: a form of stage dance; its final vowel is pronounced, unlike the light final vowel of ballot
entries.definitionCN: 芭蕾舞；词尾元音要读出来，而目标词的词尾元音很轻。

entries.definition: a French verse form; it has an extra final letter and a different stress
entries.definitionCN: 一种法语诗体；词尾多一个字母，重音也不同。

entries.definition: the general act of expressing a choice in an election or meeting
entries.definitionCN: 在选举或会议中表达选择的统称。

entries.definition: the count of votes, or a survey of public opinion
entries.definitionCN: 票数统计，或对民意的调查。

entries.definition: a direct vote on a political question, often one about sovereignty
entries.definitionCN: 就政治问题举行的直接投票，常涉及主权归属。

entries.definition: a vote on one specific question put to the whole electorate
entries.definitionCN: 就某一个具体问题交给全体选民表决的投票。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real object behind the word, real compounds and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：词背后的真实物件、真实的复合词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: The original ballot was a little ball: a voter dropped it into a box so no one could see which side it stood for.
normal.cn: 最早的选票是一颗小球：投票人把它投进箱子，谁也看不见它代表哪一边。

normal.en: Ballot box and ballot paper split the object in two: the container keeps the slips, the paper carries the choice.
normal.cn: 投票箱与选票纸把这件东西分成两半：箱子装纸片，纸片承载选择。

normal.en: Secret ballot is the fixed phrase that names the method; adding secret turns the object into a procedure.
normal.cn: 不记名投票是固定说法，加上「秘密的」这个修饰，就把物件变成了程序。

normal.en: The verb ballot means to send a question to a vote, and the prefix re- means to send it a second time.
normal.cn: 动词形式表示把问题交给投票；加上表示「再次」的前缀，就是再投一次。

normal.en: On the ballot simply means that a name or a question has reached the list voters will see.
normal.cn: 「列入选票」这个说法，意思是一个名字或问题已经进入选民会看到的那份名单。

abstract.en: Picture a ball dropped into a dark box: the hand is hidden, and only the sound of one small object falling is heard.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗球落进暗箱：手被遮住，只听得见一个小东西落下的声音。

abstract.en: Secrecy is the whole invention: the box hides the hand, and the paper hides the name.
abstract.cn: 保密正是这项发明的全部：箱子藏住手，纸片藏住名字。

abstract.en: So a ballot makes a choice countable but not traceable: the count is public, the chooser is not.
abstract.cn: 所以它让选择可以计数、却无法追溯：计数是公开的，选择者不是。

examples.en: Citizens cast their ballots before work.
examples.cn: 市民上班前投了票。

examples.en: The ballot paper was folded twice before it went into the box.
examples.cn: 选票纸折了两折才放进箱子。

examples.en: The club balloted its members on the change of meeting night.
examples.cn: 俱乐部就更改集会日期让会员投票。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「巴洛特」——把小球投进暗箱，谁也不知道你选了谁 → 无记名投票

root: 经法语上溯到意大利语 ballotta（小球），其更早来源一般追溯到原始日耳曼语中表示「球」的重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one object: a little ball dropped into a box, then the paper that replaces it, then the count and the right that grow out of that paper.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一样东西展开：先是一颗投进箱子的小球，接着是取代它的纸片，再由这张纸生出计数与权利。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small ball goes into a sealed box, and the choice is counted without being traced.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗小球落进封口的箱子，选择被计数却不被追溯。

branches.en: HIDDEN CHOICE: secret voting and drawing lots both hide the deciding hand inside a container.
branches.cn: 藏起选择：不记名投票与抽签都把做决定的手藏进容器里。

branches.en: ONE PAPER AND THE WHOLE COUNT: the slip carries a single choice, while the total turns those slips into a result.
branches.cn: 一张纸与全部票数：纸片承载单个选择，总数则把这些纸片变成一个结果。

branches.en: RIGHT AND PROCEDURE: the right to vote is exercised through the act of balloting a group.
branches.cn: 权利与程序：投票权正是通过让一群人投票这一程序来行使的。

branches.en: THE MENU: the same word also names the candidates among whom a choice is made.
branches.cn: 选项单：这个词也指供人挑选的候选人名单。

branches.en: CASTING THE PAPER: the verb names the act of marking a ballot and putting it in the box.
branches.cn: 投下纸片：动词指的是在选票上作记号并把它放进票箱的动作。

intro.en: Ballot is a borrowed noun, so its English family grows from compounds and the agent suffix rather than from a Latin root.
intro.cn: 这个词是借入的名词，所以它在英语里的词族靠复合词与表示人的后缀扩展，而不是靠拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: There is no reliable Latin family for ballot; the deeper source of the Italian word is generally traced to a reconstructed Germanic word for a ball. The formations below are English, and the Italian origin is told in the history section.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族；那个意大利词的更深来源一般追溯到原始日耳曼语中表示「球」的重构形式。下面列出的是英语中的构词，意大利语来源已在词源部分说明。

items.structure: ballot + -er (agent suffix: one who does the action)
items.meaning: a person who votes by ballot
items.meaningCN: 投票人（后缀表示「做某事的人」，语义从动作转到施事者）
items.example: Every balloter must sign the roll.
items.exampleCN: 每位投票人都必须在名册上签名。

items.meaning: the act of voting by ballot
items.meaningCN: 无记名投票这一行为（后缀把动词变成表示动作的名词）
items.example: Balloting lasted from morning until dusk.
items.exampleCN: 投票从早晨一直进行到黄昏。

items.meaning: voted by ballot; put to a ballot
items.meaningCN: 已以无记名方式投票的；被付诸表决的（后缀表示过去或被动）
items.example: The proposal was balloted last month.
items.exampleCN: 这项提议上个月已付诸表决。

items.structure: ballot + box (compound: the second element names the container)
items.meaning: the sealed box into which ballots are dropped
items.meaningCN: 投票箱（后一成分表示容器，语义从「票」转到「装票的箱子」）
items.example: Officials carried the ballot box to the counting room.
items.exampleCN: 工作人员把投票箱搬到计票室。

items.structure: ballot + paper (compound: the second element names the material)
items.meaning: the printed sheet on which a vote is marked
items.meaningCN: 选票纸（后一成分表示纸张，语义从「投票方式」转到「承载选择的纸」）
items.example: The ballot paper listed six names.
items.exampleCN: 选票纸上列着六个名字。

items.structure: secret + ballot (compound: the first element names the quality)
items.meaning: a ballot in which each vote is hidden
items.meaningCN: 无记名投票（前一成分表示「秘密的」，语义落在投票的保密性上）
items.example: The union adopted the secret ballot long before the law required it.
items.exampleCN: 早在法律要求之前，工会就采用了无记名投票。

items.structure: ballot + measure (compound: the second element names the question)
items.meaning: a question placed on a ballot for voters to decide
items.meaningCN: 付诸公投的议案（后一成分表示「议案」，语义从投票动作转到被表决的问题）
items.example: Voters rejected the ballot measure by a wide margin.
items.exampleCN: 选民以很大差距否决了这项公投议案。

items.meaningCN: 重新投票（前缀表示「再次」，语义加在投票动作之前）
items.example: The committee had to reballot the question.
items.exampleCN: 委员会不得不就这个问题重新投票。

definition_zh: adj. （空气或天气）温和宜人的；芳香的、如香脂般舒缓的；（美俚）傻乎乎的、疯疯癫癫的
definition_en: mild and pleasantly warm; fragrant and soothing like balm; in informal American use, foolish or slightly mad
core_image: 傍晚忽然软下来的那阵空气，带着草木的香气
scene: 傍晚的空气忽然软了下来，邻居们把椅子搬到门外。The evening turned balmy, so the neighbours carried their chairs outside.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：balmy 指空气温和宜人；句意是傍晚变得暖软，邻居们把椅子搬到户外。

derivatives.zh: 用香料涂尸防腐；使留存

senses.title: Mild and pleasant
senses.definition: of air or weather, pleasantly warm and gentle
senses.definitionCN: （空气或天气）暖而不燥、柔和舒适
senses.example: It was a balmy night in early May.
senses.exampleCN: 那是五月初一个温暖宜人的夜晚。
senses.why: Balm soothes the skin, so balmy air is air that feels like a soothing ointment on the face.
senses.whyCN: 香脂能安抚皮肤，所以 balmy 的空气就是拂面如涂膏般舒适的空气。

senses.title: Fragrant and soothing
senses.definition: sweet-smelling and healing, like the resin called balm
senses.definitionCN: 气味芬芳、有疗愈感，如名为香脂的树脂
senses.example: A balmy scent rose from the crushed leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 揉碎的叶片升起一股芳香。
senses.why: This is the older sense, closest to the noun balm and its scented oil.
senses.whyCN: 这是较古的义项，最贴近名词 balm 及其香油。

senses.title: Foolish or odd
senses.definition: in informal American spelling, slightly mad or silly, overlapping with barmy
senses.definitionCN: 美式非正式拼写中意为有点疯、有点傻，与 barmy 交叠
senses.example: That plan is balmy, and you know it.
senses.exampleCN: 那计划傻得很，你自己也清楚。
senses.why: Barmy came from barm, the froth on fermenting beer, and the two words converged in sound and slang use.
senses.whyCN: barmy 出自 barm「发酵啤酒上的泡沫」，两词在读音与俚语用法上合流。

intro.en: Balmy is balm plus -y. Balm travelled a long road from a Hebrew spice name through Greek, Latin and French before English turned it into an adjective about the weather.
intro.cn: balmy 是 balm 加 -y。balm 走过很长的路：从希伯来语的香料名，经希腊语、拉丁语、法语，最后被英语变成描写天气的形容词。

items.en: Hebrew basam names a spice plant, the source of a costly scented oil.
items.cn: 希伯来语 basam 指一种香料植物，是昂贵香油的来源。

items.en: Greek balsamon carries the word west as the name of the resin and its scent.
items.cn: 希腊语 balsamon 把该词西传，指树脂及其香气。

items.en: Latin balsamum keeps the sense of a healing ointment used on wounds.
items.cn: 拉丁语 balsamum 保留「敷伤口的疗伤油膏」之义。

items.en: Old French basme drops the middle sound, giving Middle English baume, later balm.
items.cn: 古法语 basme 省去中间音，产生中古英语 baume，后作 balm。

items.en: English adds -y to make balmy, first meaning fragrant and soothing like balm.
items.cn: 英语加 -y 造出 balmy，初义为「如香脂般芳香宜人」。

items.en: The sense widens to mild pleasant air, and a slang use overlaps with barmy, foolish.
items.cn: 词义扩展为空气温和宜人；俚语义与 barmy「傻」交叠。

note.en: The look-alike group puts barmy first because it sounds identical but means foolish; the near-meaning group lists the ordinary weather words balmy competes with.
note.cn: 形近组把 barmy 放在首位，因为它读音相同却意为「傻」；近义组列出与 balmy 竞争的常用天气词。

entries.definition: Slightly mad, from the froth on beer.
entries.definitionCN: 有点疯的，源自啤酒泡沫。

entries.definition: A scented healing ointment.
The inner hand, or a tropical tree.
Quiet and without wind or agitation.
Not harsh or severe.
Soft and kind in action or effect.
Of climate, moderate throughout.
Calming and easing discomfort.

normalIntro.en: Balmy is balm plus -y: air that feels like healing ointment on your face.
normalIntro.cn: balmy 就是 balm「香脂」加 -y：拂在脸上像涂了疗伤膏一样的空气。

normal.en: Balm is the soothing salve in a small tin.
normal.cn: balm 是小铁盒里那盒舒缓药膏。

normal.en: Add -y and the salve becomes a quality of the air.
normal.cn: 加上 -y，药膏就变成了空气的一种质地。

normal.en: A balmy evening needs no jacket.
normal.cn: balmy 的傍晚不必穿外套。

normal.en: Balmier and balmiest keep the y as i.
normal.cn: 比较级 balmier、最高级 balmiest 把 y 变 i。

normal.en: Do not mix it with barmy, which means silly.
normal.cn: 别与 barmy 混淆，后者意为傻。

abstract.en: Weather that behaves like kindness.
abstract.cn: 像善意一样行事的天气。

abstract.en: Warmth with the sting taken out.
abstract.cn: 被抽走了刺的暖。

abstract.en: A scent that repairs instead of demanding.
abstract.cn: 一种修补而非索取的香气。

examples.en: We ate outside because the air was balmy.
examples.cn: 我们在户外吃饭，因为空气和煦。

examples.en: A balmy smell of pine filled the whole room.
examples.cn: 满室都是松木的芳香。

examples.en: The balmiest days came late that autumn.
examples.cn: 那年秋末才出现最温和的日子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「巴蜜」——空气甜软得像蜜，就是 balmy 温和宜人的。字形上记 balm「香膏」+ -y：像涂了香膏一样舒服的空气。注意与 barmy「傻」区分。

root: balm 上溯希伯来语 basam「香料」，经希腊语 balsamon、拉丁语 balsamum、古法语 basme 进入中古英语作 baume。约 1500 年英语加 -y 造出 balmy，初指芳香如香脂，17 世纪转指空气温和；美式俚语义与 barmy「傻」合流。

sensesIntro.en: The first two senses are one idea felt on the skin and in the nose; the third is a slang accident that shares the same sound.
sensesIntro.cn: 前两个义项是同一个念头，分别落在皮肤与鼻子上；第三个是读音相同带来的俚语偶然。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: evening air softening while a scented leaf is crushed in the hand
core.cn: 核心意象：傍晚空气变软，手里揉碎一片香叶

branches.en: Chairs carried out to the pavement.
A window left open all night.
Resin warming on a fingertip.
branches.cn: 指尖上被体温融开的树脂。

branches.en: A scheme nobody sane would try.
branches.cn: 清醒的人不会试的计划。

branches.en: Comfort arriving through the skin.

intro.en: Balmy is the noun balm plus the adjective suffix -y; the comparison endings then change y to i.
intro.cn: balmy 是名词 balm 加形容词后缀 -y；比较级词尾随后把 y 变成 i。

latinIntro.en: The learned layer is balsamum and unguentum, the Latin names for scented resin and for ointment in general.
latinIntro.cn: 书面层次是 balsamum 与 unguentum，分别是拉丁语中香树脂与油膏的通名。

latinEntries.exampleCN: lenis 是 lenient 的来源。

definition_zh: 竹子；竹材
definition_en: a tall tropical grass with hard hollow stems
core_image: 一片细长的竹子站在坡上，节节分明，叶子在风里轻响
scene: 坡上长着一片细长的竹子，节节分明，叶子在风里轻响。The fence is made of bamboo.
sceneCN: 这里 bamboo 是「竹子」（第 01 个义项）；句意是篱笆是用竹子做的。

derivatives.zh: 由 bamboo 与 shoot 复合，义为「竹笋」
由 bamboo 与 grove 复合，义为「竹林」
由 bamboo 与 flute 复合，义为「竹笛」

senses.title: The tall hollow grass with jointed stems
senses.definition: a tall tropical grass with hollow, jointed stems
senses.definitionCN: 茎中空有节、长得高大的禾本科植物
senses.example: A bamboo grove stands behind the house.
senses.exampleCN: 屋后有一片竹林。
senses.why: Bamboo came into English through Portuguese and Dutch from a Malay word, and it names the tall jointed grass itself.
senses.whyCN: bamboo 经葡萄牙语和荷兰语从马来语进入英语，指这种高大、有节的禾草。

senses.title: The stems used as a material
senses.definition: the stems of this plant used as building or craft material
senses.definitionCN: 把这种植物的茎当材料使用
senses.example: The fence is made of bamboo.
senses.exampleCN: 篱笆是用竹子做的。
senses.why: Once the cut stems are used to build or make things, the plant's name also means the material taken from it.
senses.whyCN: 砍下来的竹竿一旦用来搭盖、制作，植物的名字也就指取自它的材料。

intro.en: The history of bamboo is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: bamboo 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: The word came through Portuguese bambu.
items.cn: 这个词经葡萄牙语 bambu 传入。

items.en: The Portuguese form came from a Malay word.
items.cn: 葡萄牙语形式来自马来语。

items.en: Some trace it to a Kannada word for bamboo.
items.cn: 有人认为它源自卡纳达语中指竹子的词。

items.en: Bamboo entered English in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: bamboo 在十六世纪进入英语。

items.en: It names the plant, its stems and its shoots.
items.cn: 现代英语中它指竹子、竹材与竹笋。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words close in form, root or spelling; the near-meaning group collects words from the same everyday field.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写、词根或构词相近的词；近义组收同一日常语义场里的词。

entries.definition: A word that stands close to bamboo in form or root.
A word that stands close to bamboo in form or root.
A word that stands close to bamboo in form or root.
A word that stands close to bamboo in meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 芦苇，同为细长禾本科植物。

entries.definition: A word that stands close to bamboo in meaning.
A word that stands close to bamboo in meaning.

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the word's real partners: its fixed phrase, its family, its recorded origin and its closest field.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子都建立在真实材料上：固定搭配、词族、可查的词源与最近的语义场。

normal.en: The fixed phrase 'bamboo shoot' gives the word one clear home.
normal.cn: 固定搭配「bamboo shoot」给了这个词一个清楚的落点。

normal.en: The family word 'bamboo shoot' shows how the meaning extends.
normal.cn: 词族里的「bamboo shoot」展示了词义如何向外延伸。

normal.en: Its recorded origin passes through PORTUGUESE BAMBU and MALAY.
normal.cn: 可查的来源经过 PORTUGUESE BAMBU 与 MALAY 两个阶段。

normal.en: In the same field sits 'reed'; compare the two when you recall the word.
normal.cn: 同一语义场里还有「reed」，回想时把两者放在一起比较。

normal.en: The form 'bamboos' is what you will meet in running text.
normal.cn: 在连续文本里，你常遇到的形式是「bamboos」。

abstract.en: Picture tall slender bamboo on a slope, clear joints, leaves rustling in the wind, then let the picture change size until it covers both the everyday object and the figurative use.
abstract.cn: 想象一片细长的竹子站在坡上，节节分明，叶子在风里轻响，再让画面变大变小，直到它同时罩住日常实物与比喻用法。

abstract.en: Place the word inside the scene given in this entry; what stays in memory is the picture, not the translation.
abstract.cn: 把 bamboo 放进本词条给出的场景里；留在记忆里的是画面，不是翻译。

abstract.en: Link the word to one object you can point at, then to the idea that object lends to the other senses.
abstract.cn: 把 bamboo 与一件能指认的具体事物挂钩，再挂到该事物借给其他义项的那层意思。

examples.en: A bamboo grove stands behind the house.
examples.cn: 屋后有一片竹林。

examples.en: The fence is made of bamboo.
examples.cn: 篱笆是用竹子做的。

examples.en: She keeps her pens in a bamboo cup.
examples.cn: 她把笔插在一只竹筒里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「班布」——联想到一片细长的竹子站在坡上，节节分明，叶子在风里轻响

root: 经葡萄牙语 bambu 传入英语，更早来自马来语，也有说法追溯到卡纳达语。

sensesIntro.en: Bamboo is the tall jointed grass, and also the stems of that plant used as material.
sensesIntro.cn: bamboo 指这种高大有节的竹子，也指用作材料的竹竿。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: tall slender bamboo on a slope, clear joints, leaves rustling in the wind

branches.en: PLANT: jointed stems on a green slope.

branches.en: GROVE: leaves rustling in the wind.

branches.en: FENCE: cut stems lashed together.
branches.cn: 竹材线：绑成篱笆的竹竿。

branches.en: CRAFT: a cup carved from a stem.

branches.en: STEMS: the living plant and the cut material.

definition_zh: 乐队；带子；一伙人；波段
definition_en: a group of musicians, a thin strip, or a group of people
core_image: 手腕上一根细橡皮带勒出浅痕
scene: 巷口的排练房传出鼓声。The band played three songs before the rain came.
sceneCN: 这里 band 是「乐队」（第 1 个义项：一起演奏音乐的一组人）；句意是乐队在雨来之前演奏了三首歌。

derivatives.zh: 同源词，由 band 加 -age 构成，义为「绷带」
由 band 加 -ed 构成，义为「有条纹的」
由 band 加 -ing 构成，义为「条带分布」

senses.title: A group of musicians
senses.definition: a group of people who play music together
senses.definitionCN: 一起演奏音乐的一群人
senses.example: The band played three songs before the rain came.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队在雨来之前演奏了三首歌。
senses.why: A band first meant a group bound together, and musicians who play as one unit took the name.
senses.whyCN: band 最初指被系在一起的一群人，作为一个整体演奏的乐手就用了这个称呼。

senses.title: A thin strip
senses.definition: a thin flat strip of material that ties or circles something
senses.definitionCN: 用来捆扎或环绕的细长扁条
senses.example: She tied the letters with a rubber band.
senses.exampleCN: 她用橡皮筋把信件捆好。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a strip that binds, from Old French bande, and this is the source of bandage.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是用于捆扎的带子，来自古法语 bande，也是 bandage 的来源。

senses.title: A group of people
senses.definition: a small group of people with a shared purpose
senses.definitionCN: 有共同目的的一小群人
senses.example: A band of travellers stopped at the inn.
senses.exampleCN: 一伙旅人在客栈停下。
senses.why: People bound by a common aim form a band, the same idea of tying that gives the musical group.
senses.whyCN: 因共同目标而系在一起的人就构成一伙，这和乐队的「系在一起」是同一个思路。

intro.en: Band has two old sources, one for a strip and one for a group.
intro.cn: band 有两个古老来源，一个指带子，一个指人群。

items.en: bande meant 'a strip or ribbon'.
items.cn: bande 意为「带子、饰带」。

items.en: band meant 'a band that ties'.
items.cn: band 意为「用来捆扎的带子」。

items.en: band covered strips and groups.
items.cn: band 涵盖带子与人群。

items.en: band named a group of musicians.
items.cn: band 指一群乐手。

items.en: band also means a range of signals.
items.cn: 如今 band 也指信号的波段。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one vowel; the near-meaning group gives groups and strips.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个元音；近义组是群体与条状物的说法。

normalIntro.cn: band 把东西系在一起，无论是带子还是一群演奏者。

normal.en: The plural is bands.
normal.cn: 复数是 bands。

normal.en: A rubber band stretches.
normal.cn: 橡皮筋能拉伸。

normal.en: A rock band plays music.
normal.cn: 摇滚乐队演奏音乐。

normal.en: A band of people is a small group.
normal.cn: a band of people 是一小伙人。

normal.en: The past tense is banded.
normal.cn: 过去式是 banded。

abstract.en: See a group walking together on a road.

sensesIntro.en: A strip that binds and a group bound together are the same idea of tying.
sensesIntro.cn: 捆扎用的带子与被系在一起的一群人，是同一个「系」的概念。

intro.en: The -age suffix turns band into bandage, a strip for a wound.
intro.cn: 后缀 -age 把 band 变成 bandage，即包扎伤口的带子。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; the word came from French and Norse.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，这个词来自法语与诺斯语。

definition_zh: n. 土匪；山贼；强盗（尤指结帮在偏远地区抢劫者）；掠夺者、趁机牟利者；（俚）老虎机
definition_en: a member of a gang of robbers, especially in remote or mountainous areas; a person who takes unfairly from others; in slang, a slot machine
core_image: 山口驿车旁那个用布蒙住下半脸、伸手去拿钱袋的人
scene: 山口的驿车又被拦下了，押车的看见有人抢走了钱袋。The stagecoach was stopped at the pass again, and the guard saw a bandit take the money bag.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bandit 指结帮抢劫的土匪；句意是驿车在山口被拦，押车人看见土匪抢走钱袋。

senses.title: A mountain robber
senses.definition: a member of an armed gang that robs travellers in remote country
senses.definitionCN: 在偏远地区结帮抢劫行人的武装团伙成员
senses.example: Bandits held the road above the valley for two winters.
senses.exampleCN: 土匪把山谷上方那条路把持了两个冬天。
senses.why: The Italian source meant a banished man, so the word first named someone pushed outside the law who then lived by robbery.
senses.whyCN: 意大利语词源意为「被放逐者」，所以该词起初指被逐出法律之外、转而靠抢劫为生的人。

senses.title: Anyone who preys
senses.definition: a person or firm that takes money or advantage unfairly
senses.definitionCN: 不公平地取财或取利的人或公司
senses.example: The papers called the lenders bandits in plain suits.
senses.exampleCN: 报纸把那些放贷者称作穿西装的掠夺者。
senses.why: The mountain road is replaced by a market, but the shape of the act is the same: taking by force of position.
senses.whyCN: 山路换成了市场，但行为的形状不变：凭位置之便强取。

senses.title: A slot machine
senses.definition: in the phrase one-armed bandit, a gambling machine worked by a single lever
senses.definitionCN: 用于 one-armed bandit 一语，指靠单根拉杆操作的赌博机
senses.example: He fed his wages into a one-armed bandit.
senses.exampleCN: 他把工钱全喂进了老虎机。
senses.why: The lever is the arm and the loss is the robbery, so the slang name is a small joke built on the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉杆是那条「臂」，输钱就是被「抢」，所以这个俚语名是建立在第一义上的小玩笑。

intro.en: Bandit comes from Italian bandito, a banished man. The whole family grows out of an old Germanic word for a ruler public command.
intro.cn: bandit 出自意大利语 bandito「被放逐者」。整个词族都长自一个古老的日耳曼语词，意为君主公开发布的命令。

items.en: Frankish ban meant a public command issued by a ruler, with a penalty attached.
items.cn: 法兰克语 ban 指君主公开发布的命令，附有罚则。

items.en: Late Latin bannum takes the word in as an official proclamation or summons.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 bannum 吸收该词，指官方公告或传唤。

items.en: Italian bando means a ban, and bandire means to proclaim or to banish.
items.cn: 意大利语 bando 意为禁令，bandire 意为宣告或放逐。

items.en: Italian bandito names the banished man, an outlaw living outside the law.
items.cn: 意大利语 bandito 指被放逐者，即生活在法律之外的亡命之徒。

items.en: English borrows the word for a mountain robber, with banditti as the plural at first.
items.cn: 英语借入该词指山中强盗，起初复数作 banditti。

items.en: The word widens to any predator, and a slot machine earns the name one-armed bandit.
items.cn: 词义扩为任何掠夺者；老虎机得名「独臂强盗」。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the band- family, including bandolier, which belongs to the same armed world; the near-meaning group ranks the robbery words from old to plain.
note.cn: 形近组保留 band- 词族，其中 bandolier 也属于同一个武装场景；近义组把抢劫类词按由古到今排列。

entries.definition: A strip of cloth binding a wound.
To exchange remarks carelessly or quarrelsomely.
A narrow band worn round the head.
A belt over the shoulder holding cartridges.
entries.definitionCN: 斜挎肩上装子弹的带子。

entries.definition: A member of a robber band in wild country.
entries.definitionCN: 荒野地带劫匪团伙的成员。

entries.definition: A person excluded from legal protection.
entries.definitionCN: 被排除在法律保护之外的人。

entries.definition: Someone who steals by force or threat.
entries.definitionCN: 以暴力或威胁行窃的人。

entries.definition: Someone who roams about attacking and looting.

normalIntro.en: Bandit sits inside ban: a man under the ban has been put outside the law, and that is exactly what a bandit is.
normalIntro.cn: bandit 里藏着 ban「禁令」：被下了禁令的人已被逐出法律之外，而这正是 bandit 的本相。

normal.en: Ban means an official order against someone.
normal.cn: ban 指针对某人的官方禁令。

normal.en: Italian bandito is the man the ban has fallen on.
normal.cn: 意大利语 bandito 就是被禁令落到头上的那个人。

normal.en: Cut off from law, he takes to the hills.
normal.cn: 与法律断绝后，他上了山。

normal.en: Bandits is the everyday plural; banditti is the old Italian one.
normal.cn: bandits 是日常复数，banditti 是旧的意大利式复数。

normal.en: A one-armed bandit robs you with a lever instead of a knife.
normal.cn: one-armed bandit 用拉杆而非刀子抢你。

abstract.en: A person the law has spat out and cannot swallow again.
abstract.cn: 一个被法律吐出、再也吞不回去的人。

abstract.en: Power without a uniform.
abstract.cn: 没有制服的权力。

abstract.en: A machine dressed as a game, doing the work of a robber.
abstract.cn: 装扮成游戏、干着强盗活计的机器。

examples.en: The bandits released the merchants but kept the mules.
examples.cn: 土匪放了商人，却把骡子留下。

examples.en: Travellers avoided the pass because of bandit attacks.
examples.cn: 行旅因土匪袭击而绕开那条山口。

examples.en: He lost a week of pay on a one-armed bandit.
examples.cn: 他在老虎机上输掉了一周的工钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：band（源自 ban「禁令」）+ -it——被禁令逐出的人就是 bandit 土匪。串起来记：ban 禁令 → bandito 被逐者 → bandit 山贼 → one-armed bandit 老虎机。

root: 上溯法兰克语 ban「君主公告、罚则」，经晚期拉丁语 bannum、意大利语 bando「禁令」与 bandire「宣告、放逐」，产生过去分词 bandito「被放逐者」。英语约 1590 年代借作 bandit，初以 banditti 为复数；19 世纪扩指一切掠夺者，20 世纪又生出老虎机的俚语义。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses, one shape: someone outside the rules taking what he wants, on a mountain road, in a market, or behind a lever.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项，一个形状：规则之外的人拿走他想要的东西——在山路上，在市场里，或在一根拉杆背后。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a masked figure at a mountain pass reaching for the money bag
core.cn: 核心意象：山口一个蒙面人伸手去拿钱袋

branches.en: A stopped coach in a narrow pass.
branches.cn: 窄山口里被拦下的驿车。

branches.en: A camp above the treeline.
A lender with a polite letter.
branches.cn: 寄来客套信件的放贷者。

branches.en: A lever pulled and coins gone.
Taking from outside the rules.

intro.en: Bandit keeps the Germanic ban at its centre; the Italian participle ending and the English noun suffixes build the rest of the family.
intro.cn: bandit 的核心是日耳曼语的 ban；意大利语分词词尾与英语名词后缀构成这个词族的其余部分。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin bannum and bannire form the bridge from a Frankish command to the Italian verb that produced bandito.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁语 bannum 与 bannire 是从法兰克语「命令」到意大利语动词、再到 bandito 的桥梁。

latinEntries.exampleCN: latro 在拉丁语中意为强盗。

definition_zh: n. 班卓琴（圆形鼓身、蒙皮拨弦乐器）；班卓琴声、班卓琴曲；（澳新俚）铲子、平底锅（因其形似）
definition_en: a plucked string instrument with a circular drum-like body covered by a skin; its sound or a tune for it; in Australian slang, a shovel or frying pan
core_image: 门廊上那面绷着皮的小圆鼓，鼓面上横过五根弦
scene: 门廊上那位老人拨起琴弦，鼓面般的琴身嗡嗡作响。On the porch the old man struck the strings, and the banjo answered with a bright ring.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：banjo 指班卓琴这件乐器；句意是老人在门廊拨弦，琴身发出明亮的鸣响。

senses.title: The instrument
senses.definition: a plucked instrument with a round body covered by a stretched skin and a long fretted neck
senses.definitionCN: 一种拨弦乐器，圆形琴身蒙着绷紧的皮，琴颈长而有品
senses.example: His banjo had a skin head worn pale at the centre.
senses.exampleCN: 他那把班卓琴的皮面中央已磨得发白。
senses.why: The body is a small drum, which is why the instrument rings rather than hums like a wooden guitar.
senses.whyCN: 琴身其实是一面小鼓，所以它的声音是「叮」而不是木吉他那种「嗡」。

senses.title: Its sound or tune
senses.definition: the bright ringing tone of the instrument, or a piece written for it
senses.definitionCN: 这件乐器明亮带金属感的音色，或为它写的曲子
senses.example: A banjo carried the melody over the fiddles.
senses.exampleCN: 班卓琴声压过提琴，担起了主旋律。
senses.why: As with other instruments, the name can stand for the sound produced rather than the object held.
senses.whyCN: 与其他乐器一样，这个名字可以代指发出的声音，而不是抱在手里的实物。

senses.title: A shaped tool
senses.definition: in Australian and New Zealand slang, a shovel or frying pan, from the round shape
senses.definitionCN: 澳新俚语中指铲子或平底锅，取名于其圆形
senses.example: He grabbed the banjo and started clearing the drain.
senses.exampleCN: 他抓起铲子开始清理排水沟。
senses.why: Slang often names a tool after an object it resembles, and the round blade matches the round drum body.
senses.whyCN: 俚语常用形似之物给工具起名，圆铲面正对应圆鼓琴身。

intro.en: Banjo is an American word with two possible ancestors: an African gourd lute carried across the Atlantic, and an old Mediterranean lute name. Both threads meet in the colonial South.
intro.cn: banjo 是一个美国词，有两个可能的祖先：被带过大西洋的非洲葫芦琴，以及古老的地中海琉特琴名。两条线在殖民地时期的美国南方交汇。

items.en: Greek pandoura names an old three-stringed lute of the eastern Mediterranean.
items.cn: 希腊语 pandoura 指东地中海一种古老的三弦琉特琴。

items.en: Portuguese bandorre and Spanish bandurria carry the lute name to the Atlantic world.
items.cn: 葡萄牙语 bandorre 与西班牙语 bandurria 把这一琴名带到大西洋世界。

items.en: Kimbundu mbanza names a plucked gourd instrument brought across the Atlantic by enslaved people.
items.cn: 金邦杜语 mbanza 指一种拨奏葫芦琴，由被奴役者带过大西洋。

items.en: Colonial writers record banza and banjer in the Caribbean and the American South.
items.cn: 殖民地文献在加勒比与美国南方记下 banza 与 banjer 等写法。

items.en: The spelling banjo settles in American English for the drum-bodied plucked instrument.
items.cn: 拼写 banjo 在美式英语中固定，指鼓身拨弦乐器。

items.en: Minstrel stages and later bluegrass make it a national sound, and slang borrows its shape.
items.cn: 游艺舞台与后来的蓝草音乐使它成为标志性声音，俚语又借其形状取义。

note.en: The look-alike group starts with bongo, another drum name, then moves to unrelated ban- words; the near-meaning group is the plucked-instrument family the banjo belongs to.
note.cn: 形近组以另一个鼓名 bongo 开头，随后转向无关的 ban- 词；近义组是班卓琴所属的拨弦乐器家族。

entries.definition: One of a pair of small hand drums.
A rigid ring worn as jewellery.
A fig tree whose branches root themselves.
A Japanese shout of acclaim.
A small lute with four pairs of strings.
entries.definitionCN: 装有四对弦的小琉特琴。

entries.definition: A small four-stringed Hawaiian guitar.
A fretted string instrument with a wooden body.
entries.definitionCN: 木质琴身的有品弦乐器。

entries.definition: An old plucked instrument with a rounded back.
entries.definitionCN: 背部圆凸的古老拨弦乐器。

normalIntro.en: Picture a frying pan with strings across it: that is a banjo, and the same picture explains the Australian slang.
normalIntro.cn: 想象一只平底锅上横着几根弦：那就是 banjo；同一幅画面也解释了澳洲俚语里的「铲子」。

normal.en: The body is a little drum, not a wooden box.
normal.cn: 琴身是一面小鼓，不是木箱。

normal.en: Five strings run over a stretched skin.
normal.cn: 五根弦横过一张绷紧的皮。

normal.en: Banjos is the usual plural; banjoes also exists.
normal.cn: banjos 是常用复数，banjoes 也存在。

normal.en: A banjoist is the player, as a guitarist plays guitar.
normal.cn: banjoist 是琴手，正如 guitarist 弹吉他。

normal.en: In Australian slang the round shovel is also a banjo.
normal.cn: 澳洲俚语里圆头铲子也叫 banjo。

abstract.en: A drum that learned to sing notes.

definition_zh: 破产（无力清偿债务的法律状态或司法程序）
definition_en: the legal state or procedure of being unable to pay one's debts
core_image: 一张被砸断的长凳，木片散落在钱币兑换商的门前
scene: 订单断了三个月后，这家工厂向法院申请破产，债权人开始登记申报。After three months without orders, the factory filed for bankruptcy, and its creditors began to register their claims.
sceneCN: 这里指「因无力偿债而进入的法律程序」（第 1 个义项：经法院处理的破产状态）；句意为断单三个月后，这家工厂向法院申请破产，债权人开始登记申报。可辨识物件：断凳、法院门牌、债权登记表、封条。

senses.title: The legal status of being unable to pay
senses.titleCN: 无力清偿债务的法律状态
senses.definition: the formal condition, recognised by a court, in which a debtor cannot meet its debts
senses.definitionCN: 经法院认定、债务人无法履行债务的正式状态
senses.example: The court placed the firm in bankruptcy after the payment deadline passed.
senses.exampleCN: 付款期限过后，法院使这家企业进入破产状态。
senses.why: the word began as a broken bench, so the legal status keeps the image of a trader put out of business.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本指被砸断的长凳，法律状态因此保留商人被逐出营业的意象。

senses.title: Liquidation of the debtor's assets
senses.titleCN: 变卖债务人资产以清偿
senses.definition: the procedure in which assets are sold and the proceeds divided among creditors
senses.definitionCN: 变卖资产并把所得分给债权人的程序
senses.example: Bankruptcy ended with the mill sold and the workers paid first.
senses.exampleCN: 破产以工厂被出售、工人先获清偿而结束。
senses.why: if the business cannot continue, the assets must be turned into money so creditors can be paid in order.
senses.whyCN: 企业若无法继续，资产必须换成钱，债权人才能按顺序获偿。

senses.title: Reorganisation instead of sale
senses.definition: a procedure that keeps the business running while debts are restructured
senses.definitionCN: 在重组债务的同时让企业继续运营的程序
senses.example: The airline used bankruptcy to renegotiate its leases, not to close.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司借破产重新谈租约，而非关门。
senses.why: a business may be worth more alive than sold, so the law offers a route that keeps it running while debts are rebuilt.
senses.whyCN: 企业活着可能比卖掉更值钱，法律因此提供一条让它继续运营、同时重组债务的路径。

senses.title: Personal bankruptcy
senses.definition: the same legal route taken by an individual rather than a company
senses.definitionCN: 由个人而非企业走上的同一法律路径
senses.example: Personal bankruptcy cleared the medical debts but ruined her credit.
senses.exampleCN: 个人破产免除了医疗债务，却毁了她的信用。
senses.why: a person can owe more than he owns just as a company can, so the same procedure is offered to individuals.
senses.whyCN: 个人也会像企业一样欠得比拥有的多，同一程序因此也向个人开放。

senses.title: The figurative collapse of an idea or system
senses.titleCN: 观念或体系的比喻性崩解
senses.definition: a total failure of a scheme, theory or institution, without any court involved
senses.definitionCN: 计划、理论或机构的彻底失败，与法院无关
senses.example: The report described the plan as a moral and economic bankruptcy.
senses.exampleCN: 报告称该计划在道义与经济上均已破产。
senses.why: the broken bench can be imagined anywhere, so any total failure is described with the same word.
senses.whyCN: 断凳可以被想象在任何地方，任何彻底的失败便都用同一个词描述。

senses.title: Moral bankruptcy in public life
senses.titleCN: 公共生活中的道德破产
senses.definition: the loss of credibility or ethical standing of a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 个人或团体失去公信力或道德地位
senses.example: The scandal exposed the moral bankruptcy of the leadership.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻暴露出领导层的道德破产。
senses.why: when credibility rather than money is gone, the word still fits, because nothing is left to pay with.
senses.whyCN: 当失去的是公信力而非金钱时，这个词仍然合用，因为已无东西可付。

senses.title: The act of filing a petition
senses.definition: the formal step by which a debtor or creditor starts the procedure
senses.definitionCN: 债务人或债权人启动程序的形式步骤
senses.example: The filing for bankruptcy came on a Friday afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 破产申请是在一个周五下午提交的。
senses.why: the procedure begins with a document, so the act of filing is spoken of as the event itself.
senses.whyCN: 程序从一份文书开始，因此提交的动作本身被当作事件来说。

senses.title: Bankruptcy protection and the automatic stay
senses.definition: the court order that pauses collection and lawsuits while the case proceeds
senses.definitionCN: 案件进行期间暂停追债与诉讼的法院命令
senses.example: Bankruptcy protection stopped the bank from seizing the equipment.
senses.exampleCN: 破产保护阻止了银行扣押设备。
senses.why: creditors would otherwise race to seize assets, so a court order freezes collection while the case is sorted out.
senses.whyCN: 否则债权人会抢先扣押资产，法院命令因此在案件理清期间冻结追债。

senses.title: Fraudulent bankruptcy
senses.definition: the offence of hiding or transferring assets before or during insolvency
senses.definitionCN: 在无力偿付之前或期间藏匿、转移资产的罪行
senses.example: Two directors were charged with fraudulent bankruptcy.
senses.exampleCN: 两名董事被控欺诈性破产。
senses.why: hiding assets before the case defeats the purpose of the law, so the conduct is made a separate offence.
senses.whyCN: 在案发前藏匿资产会摧毁法律的目的，因此该行为被单列为罪行。

intro.en: Bankruptcy comes from Italian banca rotta 'broken bench', the table of a money changer who could not pay. The image reached English through French and Latin forms in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: bankruptcy 来自意大利语 banca rotta「被砸断的长凳」，即无力清偿的钱币兑换商的桌子。这一意象于 16 世纪经法语与拉丁形式进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: A banca was the bench or table where a money changer and his coins sat in a public square.
items.cn: banca 指钱币兑换商与他的钱币在公共广场上占据的长凳或桌子。

items.en: Rumpere meant 'to break', and its participle ruptus supplied the second half of banca rotta.
items.cn: rumpere 意为「打断」，其分词 ruptus 提供 banca rotta 的后一半。

items.en: In Italian practice a trader who could not pay might have his bench broken, a public sign that he could no longer do business.
items.cn: 在意大利的惯例中，无力清偿的商人可能被砸断长凳，公开表明他不能再做生意。

items.en: French borrowed the image as banqueroute, and English took the noun in the sixteenth century in forms such as bankrupt.
items.cn: 法语把这个意象借为 banqueroute，英语于 16 世纪以 bankrupt 一类形式吸收该名词。

items.en: The abstract noun bankruptcy was formed in English on the model of French, adding the ending that names a state or procedure.
items.cn: 抽象名词 bankruptcy 在英语中仿法语构成，加上表示状态或程序的词尾。

items.en: The nineteenth and twentieth centuries turned the image into a statute-based procedure with liquidation, reorganisation, protection and criminal forms.
items.cn: 19 与 20 世纪把这一意象变成以成文法为基础的程序，包含清算、重整、保护与犯罪形态。

note.en: Group one holds words from the broken-bench image or from breaking; group two holds legal and financial terms that are often used as if they were synonyms.
note.cn: 第一组是出自「断凳」意象或「打断」词根的词；第二组是常被当作同义词使用的法律与金融术语。

entries.definition: A debtor legally declared unable to pay, or the act of making someone so; bankruptcy is the state or case.
entries.definitionCN: 指被依法宣告无力清偿的债务人，或使某人如此的行为；bankruptcy 指状态或案件。

entries.definition: The institution that grew from the money changer's bench; the shared origin is invisible in modern use.
entries.definitionCN: 指由钱币商长凳发展而来的机构；共同的来源在现代用法中已看不出来。

entries.definition: A break or burst, often of a pipe or a relationship; it has nothing to do with money.
entries.definitionCN: 指断裂或爆裂，常用于管道或关系；与金钱无关。

entries.definition: To break into something in progress; the prefix means between, and no debt is involved.
entries.definitionCN: 指打断进行中的事情；前缀意为「在……之间」，不涉债务。

entries.definition: The accounting state of owing more than one owns; bankruptcy is the legal procedure that may follow.
entries.definitionCN: 指欠得比拥有的多的会计状态；bankruptcy 是随后可能启动的法律程序。

entries.definition: The selling off of assets; it is one form bankruptcy can take, not the whole procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 指变卖资产；它是破产可能采取的一种形式，而非整个程序。

entries.definition: Failure to pay on a due date; a default can occur without any bankruptcy case being opened.
entries.definitionCN: 指到期未付；违约可以在未启动任何破产案件时发生。

entries.definition: Control of a company given to an outside officer for creditors; it is a separate legal route.
entries.definitionCN: 指把公司控制权交给外部官员以维护债权人；是另一条法律路径。

normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：复合词的真实成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The family runs bankrupt, bankruptcy, bank, rupture, interrupt, disrupt.
normal.cn: 同族词包括破产的、破产、银行、断裂、打断、扰乱。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the steps: file for, declare, protection, proceedings.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出步骤：申请、宣布、保护、程序。

normal.en: The bench survives in bank, and the breaking survives in rupture.
normal.cn: 那张长凳留在银行一词里，打断的动作留在断裂一词里。

normal.en: A filing is not a closure: protection can keep the business alive while debts are rebuilt.

root: 意大利语 banca rotta「断凳」：banca「长凳、钱桌」加 rotta，后者出自拉丁 ruptus／rumpere「打断」。经法语 banqueroute 于 16 世纪进入英语，抽象名词仿法语构成。同根词有 rupture、interrupt、disrupt、corrupt、abrupt。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one case: the legal status, the sale of assets, the attempt to keep trading, the individual route, the collapse of an idea, moral collapse, the filing itself, the protection that pauses creditors, and the criminal form.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个案件展开：法律状态、变卖资产、设法继续经营、个人路径、观念的崩解、道德崩解、申请的动作、暂停追债的保护，以及犯罪形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a smashed bench on the stones of a market square.
core.cn: 核心意象：集市广场石板上的一张被砸断的长凳。

branches.en: STATUS AND PETITION: the condition is declared, and someone must file to start it.
branches.cn: 状态与申请：条件被宣告，且必须有人提交申请才能启动。

branches.en: TWO OUTCOMES: the assets are sold, or the business is kept alive and the debts rebuilt.
branches.cn: 两种结局：资产被变卖，或企业继续存活、债务被重组。

branches.en: THE INDIVIDUAL: a person can take the same route as a company.
branches.cn: 个人：一个人可以走与企业相同的路径。

branches.en: THE WORD WITHOUT A COURT: an idea or a leadership can be called bankrupt in plain speech.
branches.cn: 无需法院的词：观念或领导层可以在日常语言中被称为破产。

branches.en: PROTECTION AND ABUSE: the law pauses collection, and the law also punishes hidden assets.

definition_zh: 野蛮人；未开化者；粗野无礼之人
definition_en: a person seen as uncivilized or uncultured; rough and rude in behavior
core_image: 城墙外口音古怪、挥着棍棒的来客
scene: 罗马边境哨兵远远望见营火与怪叫。The barbarians gathered beyond the northern wall.
sceneCN: 这里 barbarian 指「（古时）异族入侵者」（第 1 个义项：被视为未开化之人）；句意：蛮族聚集在北墙之外。

derivatives.zh: 野蛮的；残暴的（barbarian 同根形容词）

senses.title: An outsider of another tongue
senses.definition: historically, a person whose language and customs were foreign to a classical culture
senses.definitionCN: 古代指语言习俗异于古典文明的人
senses.example: Greeks first applied the word to all non-Greek speakers.
senses.exampleCN: 希腊人最初以此词泛指一切非希腊语者。
senses.why: Greek barbaros imitated unintelligible speech: bar-bar, babbling.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 barbaros 模仿真异语言：bar-bar，如鸟语嘟哝。

senses.title: An uncivilized person
senses.definition: a person regarded as primitive or without refinement
senses.definitionCN: 被视为原始或缺乏教养的人
senses.example: The ruins told of barbarians who burned the library.
senses.exampleCN: 废墟诉说着焚毁图书馆的蛮人。
senses.why: Foreign speech slid into the idea of no culture at all.
senses.whyCN: 「异语」滑向「无文明」的成见。

senses.title: A cruel or coarse person
senses.definition: a person who behaves crudely or brutally
senses.definitionCN: 举止粗暴或残忍的人
senses.example: Only barbarians wreck a hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 只有野蛮人才会毁掉医院。
senses.why: Rudeness of tongue grew into rudeness of deed.
senses.whyCN: 语言之粗野长成行为之粗暴。

senses.title: Uncultured destruction
senses.definition: barbarian conduct, especially vandalism of culture
senses.definitionCN: 野蛮行径，尤指对文化的破坏
senses.example: The iconoclasm was pure barbarian.
senses.exampleCN: 这场毁像运动十足野蛮。
senses.why: The adjective names the classic crime of the invader.
senses.whyCN: 形容词点出入侵者的经典罪行。

senses.title: In Byzantine and Chinese usage
senses.titleCN: 拜占庭与中文里的「胡」「蛮」
senses.definition: a border peoples' label used by empires for outside groups
senses.definitionCN: 帝国对边界外族群的统称
senses.example: Byzantine records list many barbarian peoples.
senses.exampleCN: 拜占庭文献罗列众多蛮族。
senses.why: Empire names the outsider before it knows him.
senses.whyCN: 帝国在了解外人之前先给他命名。

senses.title: Modern figurative use
senses.definition: anyone indifferent to art, manners, or knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 对艺术、礼仪或知识冷漠无知之人
senses.example: Philistines and barbarians walk the same modern street.
senses.exampleCN: 市侩与蛮人行走于同一条现代街道。
senses.why: Civilization kept the word to shame its own members.
senses.whyCN: 文明留住此词，用以羞辱自己的成员。

senses.title: Adjectival barbarian style
senses.definition: of or like barbarians, rough and unrefined
senses.definitionCN: 蛮族式的，粗犷未经雕琢
senses.example: The hall had a barbarian magnificence.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅有一种蛮荒的壮丽。
senses.why: Roughness can be admired as vigor.
senses.whyCN: 粗犷亦可被视为力量而受赞赏。

senses.title: The reduplicated root elsewhere
senses.definition: related words from the same bar-bar imitation, as Barbary and Berber
senses.definitionCN: 同一拟声词根的相关词，如 Barbary、Berber
senses.example: The Barbary coast took its name from the same root.
senses.exampleCN: 巴巴里海岸之名亦出此根。
senses.why: The babbling sound named North Africans to Europeans.
senses.whyCN: 嘟哝之声被欧洲人安在北非人头上。

intro.en: Barbarian comes from Greek barbaros, whose babbling bar-bar imitated foreign speech; Latin adopted barbarus, and the Romance languages carried the word everywhere.
intro.cn: barbarian 出自希腊语 barbaros，其叠音 bar-bar 模仿外语的嘟哝声；拉丁语作 barbarus，罗曼语把它传遍各地。

items.en: The reduplicated syllable echoes unclear babbling.
items.cn: 叠音音节回响着含混的嘟哝。

items.cn: barbaros 指言语不可解者；后指未开化者。

items.en: Latin borrowed barbarus for foreign tribes beyond the frontier.
items.cn: 拉丁语借 barbarus 称边境之外的异族。

items.en: Late Latin barbarus became barbare in French.
items.cn: 后期拉丁语 barbarus 变为法语 barbare。

items.en: English took barbarian in the sixteenth century as the person-word beside barbarous.
items.cn: 英语于十六世纪取 barbarian 作指人之词，与 barbarous 并行。

items.en: Today it is chiefly figurative: anyone opposed to civilization.
items.cn: 今日主要用于比喻：一切反文明之人。

senses.title: Brutally cruel
senses.definition: shockingly cruel and without any restraint of civilised feeling

senses.title: Foreign, in old use

senses.why: This is the original Greek sense: the word first imitated speech that sounded like bar bar to Greek ears.
senses.whyCN: 这是希腊语的原义：该词最初模仿在希腊人耳中听起来像「bar bar」的话语。

intro.en: Barbaric began as an imitation of unintelligible speech: bar bar. Greek turned that sound into a word for foreign, and history turned foreign into cruel.
intro.cn: barbaric 起初是对听不懂的话语的模仿：bar bar。希腊人把这个声音变成「异族」一词，历史又把「异族」变成了「残暴」。

items.en: Greek barbaros imitates speech that sounds like bar bar, so it first meant foreign.
items.cn: 希腊语 barbaros 模仿听起来像「bar bar」的话语，初义为「异族的」。

items.en: Greek barbarikos turns the noun into an adjective, of or like foreigners.
items.cn: 希腊语 barbarikos 把名词变为形容词，意为「异族的、像异族的」。

items.en: Latin barbaricus keeps the adjective for peoples outside the empire.
items.cn: 拉丁语 barbaricus 保留该形容词，指帝国之外的族群。

items.en: English takes the word through French, still mainly meaning foreign and unpolished.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入该词，仍主要表示「异族的、未加雕琢的」。

items.en: Wars and travel writing push the word toward savage cruelty rather than mere difference.
items.cn: 战争与游记把词义推向残暴，而不再只是「不同」。

items.en: Modern use splits: barbaric marks cruelty, barbarous marks crude taste, barbarian names the person.
items.cn: 现代用法分化：barbaric 指残暴，barbarous 偏粗鄙，barbarian 指其人。

note.en: The look-alike group first separates the three barbar- relatives by what each one names, then adds two false friends; the near-meaning group grades cruelty from wild to unrefined.
note.cn: 形近组先把三个 barbar- 亲属按各自所指区分开，再加入两个假朋友；近义组把「残酷」由凶猛到粗鄙分级排列。

entries.definition: Rough and unrefined, also cruel.
entries.definitionCN: 粗鄙未开化的，也可指残暴。

entries.definition: A member of a people thought uncivilised.
entries.definitionCN: 被视为未开化族群的一员。

entries.definition: Someone who cuts hair and trims beards.
A drug that depresses the nervous system.
Violently wild and uncontrolled.
Showing no mercy or feeling.
Willing to cause suffering.
Without the manners of an ordered society.

normalIntro.en: Say bar bar aloud: that is what foreign speech sounded like to Greek ears, and barbaric is built on that stammer.
normalIntro.cn: 把 bar bar 念出声：这就是希腊人耳中异族语言的声音，而 barbaric 就建在这个「口吃」之上。

normal.en: Barbar- is the stammer, -ic is the adjective ending.
normal.cn: barbar- 是那个口吃声，-ic 是形容词词尾。

normal.en: Barbarian is the person; barbaric is the quality.
normal.cn: barbarian 指人，barbaric 指性质。

normal.en: Barbarity is the cruel act; barbarism is the crude state.
normal.cn: barbarity 指暴行，barbarism 指粗野状态。

normal.en: Barbaric has no -er form; use more barbaric.
normal.cn: barbaric 没有 -er 形式，比较级用 more barbaric。

normal.en: Barbaric splendour means rich but tasteless.
normal.cn: barbaric splendour 意为奢华却无品味。

abstract.en: A sound of not understanding, hardened into a verdict.
abstract.cn: 一声「听不懂」，硬化成了一句判词。

abstract.en: The moment difference is renamed as fault.
abstract.cn: 「不同」被改名为「过错」的那一刻。

abstract.en: Gold piled where restraint should stand.
abstract.cn: 本该站着克制的地方，堆满了金子。

examples.en: They condemned the barbaric treatment of prisoners.
examples.cn: 他们谴责对囚犯的残暴对待。

examples.en: The palace was a barbaric display of gold and mirrors.
examples.cn: 那座宫殿是金饰与镜子的粗野炫耀。

examples.en: More barbaric punishments were abolished that year.
examples.cn: 那一年废除了更野蛮的刑罚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「巴巴里克」——听不清的「巴巴」声就是词根 barbar-，加 -ic 成形容词。记一条线：bar bar 听不懂 → 异族 → 未开化 → 残暴。人叫 barbarian，性质叫 barbaric。

root: 希腊语 barbaros 模仿异族语言「bar bar」之声，初义「非希腊的、异族的」；派生 barbarikos，经拉丁语 barbaricus、法语进入英语，约 1400 年作 barbaric。17 世纪战争与游记把词义推向残暴，现代与 barbarous「粗鄙」、barbarian「其人」分工。

sensesIntro.en: Read the three senses as a history: first foreign, then unpolished, finally cruel. The order of the senses is the order of the prejudice.
sensesIntro.cn: 把三个义项当成一段历史来读：先是异族，再是无教养，最后是残暴。义项的顺序就是偏见形成的顺序。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a punishment in a closed file that belongs to no century
core.cn: 核心意象：合上的卷宗里那种不属于任何世纪的刑罚

branches.en: A sentence read out in a quiet court.
branches.cn: 安静法庭上宣读的判词。

branches.en: Gold leaf over every surface.
Ornament with no empty space.
Tribes drawn beyond the river.
branches.cn: 地图上画在河外的部落。

branches.en: A verdict passed from outside.

intro.en: Barbaric is the reduplicated root barbar- plus -ic; the same root gives the person, the act and the state through different suffixes.
intro.cn: barbaric 是叠音词根 barbar- 加 -ic；同一词根通过不同后缀分别给出「人」「行为」与「状态」。

latinIntro.en: Latin barbarus and barbaricus carry the Greek word west; brutus, heavy and dull, supplies the near-synonym brutal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 barbarus 与 barbaricus 把希腊词西传；brutus「沉重迟钝」提供近义词 brutal。
